# AIHOT news references

The news module references [KKKKhazix/AIHOT at commit c547b669acc7f64720cd82024e502446ee1ef88d](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/AIHOT/tree/c547b669acc7f64720cd82024e502446ee1ef88d), under the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2026 数字生命卡兹克. The unchanged [license text](aihot-LICENSE.txt) accompanies NAND, and [NOTICE](../../NOTICE) records the attribution.

| NAND implementation | Upstream reference | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `src/modules/news/core/materials.ts` | `packages/backend/src/content/materials.ts`, `decideTimeline` and `fillPublicationTime` | First imports, articles older than 48 hours, missing dates and dates over one hour in the future stay outside today's reading list. Later date corrections use the original discovery time. |
| `src/modules/news/core/materials.ts` | `packages/backend/src/content/materials.ts`, `contentHash` and `upsertIn` | SHA-256 of whitespace-normalized title, body and summary separated by U+0001 identifies a content revision. Omitted body/summary fields retain stored text; another source's rendering of the same canonical article cannot replace its owner. NAND also hashes source-item identity with SHA-256. |
| `src/modules/news/core/source-schedule.ts` | `packages/backend/src/sources/collect.ts`, `adaptIntervals` | Seven-day non-backfill volume determines intervals between 15 and 60 minutes, with a 180-minute ceiling for signal sources. Consecutive failures increase the delay up to 360 minutes. |
| `src/modules/news/core/scoring.ts` | `industry/selection.ts`, `industry/prompts/selection-score.md` | Seven sets of integer weights, evidence caps, tier thresholds of 60/65/76, floored display averages and the strict greater-than-50 writing rule. Raw axes remain available for local reweighting. |
| `src/modules/news/core/prompt-templates.ts` | `industry/prompts/prefilter.md`, `selection-score.md`, `structure.md`, `content-understanding.md` | Untrusted-material boundaries, event-based scoring, relevance states, category/tag vocabulary, factual frames with source quotations, and Chinese writing rules. |
| `src/modules/news/core/prompts.ts` | `packages/backend/src/editorial/prompts.ts` | Effective template/dependency hashing and explicit errors for missing variables or includes. |
| `src/modules/news/core/recall.ts`, `grouping.ts` | `packages/backend/src/events/recall.ts`, `relate.ts`, `group.ts`; `industry/prompts/group-definitions.md`, `group-method.md` | Discovery within fourteen days, title plus the first 300 summary characters, character-bigram overlap of at least 0.25, the best report per occurrence and ten candidates. Four explicit relations use a 0.8 tie threshold; developments attach directly to roots, roundups only mention events, and existing-event merges require an independent root review at 0.75. Old event IDs resolve through retained aliases. |
| `src/modules/news/core/representative.ts` | `packages/backend/src/publication/representative.ts` | Choose the occurrence with the most distinct sources, breaking ties by earlier time; within it prefer T1, matching institutional/person publishers, full text, higher score, earlier time and stable ID. |
| `src/modules/news/core/heat.ts` | `packages/backend/src/events/hot.ts`, `publication/hot.ts`; `apps/web/app/features/hot/curve.ts` | Deduplicate participants, keep their latest original publication within 48 hours, decay with a 24-hour half-life and compare against the window six hours earlier. Require two participants including one editorial participant, then show the top ten. Exclude late or stale participants from growth comparisons and use one source-coverage cohort across each historical plot. |
| `src/modules/news/core/edition.ts` | `packages/backend/src/reports/edition.ts`, `dailyMemory`, `dailyEdition`, `arrangeDaily` | One entry per event; importance is `(score ?? 50) + 5 log2(1 + participants) + official × 5 − follow-up × 6`. Keep twelve main entries, ten brief updates and at most two main entries per leading source. Remember seven days of cited occurrences, allow new party actions or four-source follow-ups in main entries, retain the all-follow-up-day exception, fold roundups under their most important mentioned event, and admit unselected official reports with three independent participants. |

NAND implements collection through Obsidian's `requestUrl`, with a bounded local service queue and device JSON stores. Visible favorites and briefs use Markdown and the Vault API. NAND does not include AIHOT's server, database, paid collectors, model API credentials, name or logo. RSS, Atom, JSON Feed and OPML parsing follows their format contracts through host DOM parsing; the static-list adapter uses user-selected CSS selectors without executing page scripts.

NAND's requested local prefilter is implemented in `core/analysis-policy.ts`: blocked terms, minimum text length and declared feed language run before new analysis calls. This is separate from the upstream editorial relevance prompt. Missing language metadata remains eligible. The configurable category/topic/entity vocabulary drives both the effective prompt hash and strict reply validation; each durable analysis plan snapshots it. The settings UI can restore the default vocabulary or all four templates and displays the effective SHA-256. These controls use NAND settings and local recovery, without introducing an upstream server dependency.

NAND batches at most twelve materials with a default 1,500-character body excerpt, additionally bounded by the serialized CLI input size. It combines relevance, raw score axes, structure, writing and candidate relations in one marked JSON response. Upstream invokes these stages separately and returns a computed attention score. NAND calculates the score locally; optional double scoring uses two independent calls. Batch-local IDs omit source identity, and the model never receives source tiers or previous scores. This batching difference still requires comparison against labeled material and real CLI answers; protocol fixtures alone do not establish editorial equivalence.

The local run journal saves a reservation before a CLI call and the full reply before applying records. Analysis, repairs, double scoring, merge reviews and briefs share the daily quota. On restart, received replies can be consumed locally; unknown started calls require an explicit retry. These execution rules use NAND's native CLI runner and private JSON storage, not AIHOT's server queue or direct model API.

NAND's lexical recall also includes earlier materials in the same batch. Each material must return exactly one verdict for each supplied candidate; missing or foreign targets fail validation. Root merge reviews run independently of the first analysis. The grouping and representative fixtures cover duplicate reports, direct developments, roundups, low confidence, source-count ties and alias recovery; the native Obsidian protocol probe covers reading, durable reviews and restart. NAND does not use embeddings, social-post reply metadata or upstream's database merge machinery.

NAND observes completed hours only while the local module is running. Startup, suspend and offline intervals leave gaps. Later collection can repair coverage in an already observed hour, but cannot create a missing hour. Seven days of observations are retained, including events below the top ten. The chart needs three complete observations, preserves gaps and labels the actual local time range; source role or ownership changes recalculate from retained evidence without a model call. Community-author identities use the configured group or source as their namespace instead of upstream source-pack names. Native chart checks use explicit historical fixtures and do not claim seven days of live monitoring.

NAND's daily edition uses the device's local calendar day instead of AIHOT's scheduled server publication at 08:00 Asia/Shanghai. Each compiled issue saves its date, time zone and exact start/end instants in device reader state. Collection, analysis or explicit compilation records the issue; reading and filtering stay local and do not call a model or write Markdown. The optional daily-note setting updates the same day's managed Markdown region and preserves annotations. Saved views store a stable ID and bounded filters; each workbench leaf keeps its own current section, filter, selection and timeline order.

The heat and edition numbers in the mapping above are defaults. NAND's `core/editorial-rules.ts` and native settings add bounded local controls for the heat window/decay, participant/list limits, comparison/badge thresholds and daily entry/source/memory limits. Saved changes recalculate retained evidence without another model call; heat rule versions identify the applied parameters. Historical charts keep their original observed hours. Published issue history retains up to 30 days, while the default edition memory remains seven days.

The upstream weekly/monthly reference ranks an event by its best score, `5 log2(1 + maximum sources)`, six points for leading, three for a highlight, and `4 × (days carried − 1)`. This is a research mapping only: NAND's current scope provides a daily edition and has no weekly/monthly product entry.

This mapping records the implemented rules. Reader workflows, home widgets and native CLI acceptance have separate requirements; this document does not certify those requirements as complete.

Material hashing uses the host's Web Crypto implementation. The old 32-bit FNV collision pair `item-1ppgtvf` / `item-rx6lxj` is retained as a regression fixture for both content revisions and source-item IDs. Previously accepted content hashes remain with the retained cache, so a feed rotating back to old text preserves the current revision instead of requesting another analysis. NAND stores these hashes in the material JSON instead of upstream's full revision-history table; clearing or expiring the cache also clears this history.
